REJUGÉE le 2026-09-03 après ldpy 0.6.3 (fiche ldpy/027). Classée not-expressible parce que les cinq Namespace locaux étaient liés au graphe PAR VALEUR. Les deux changements la débloquent, et elle montre le cas dynamique : TOUTES les IRI de cette fonction sont des valeurs d'exécution (un réglage Qt, un attribut de self), donc chaque préfixe se déclare en IRI formatée — '@prefix ifcInst: f<{base_inst}ifcInst:> as ifc_inst_ns .' — et 'as' garde l'objet, que les boucles indexent ensuite par une clé d'exécution (ifc_inst_ns[data['eq_guid']]). Les sept self.output_graph.bind() disparaissent par héritage. Un point de conception s'est révélé ici : le graphe hérite des préfixes EN PORTÉE AU MOMENT de la désignation, donc '@graph' suit maintenant les déclarations au lieu de les précéder. Casse délibérée vérifiée : FAIL puis OK.

[note antérieure] prefixes: RDF->rdf (RDF is only ever used as RDF.type here, never bound or exported -- a clean @prefix). NOT-EXPRESSIBLE (the ns_def_local target idiom, decisively so): all 5 local Namespace(...) objects this region defines (ifc_inst_ns, brick_inst_ns, bacnet_ns, bldg_ns, ifc_core_ns) are, without exception, passed BY VALUE to self.output_graph.bind(prefix, ns) a few lines later -- exactly the escape route AGENT_BATCH.md names as #3 (g.bind(prefix, NS) passes the object). `@prefix` has no run-time object (INSTRUCTIONS.md §1), so none of the 5 can become `@prefix ns: <IRI> .` without breaking the very next `.bind()` call -- same 'no partial win' situation and same convention as the sibling BONSAMURAIS__arborist__..._setup_empty_graph in this stratum: kept as plain Namespace(...), unchanged, rather than doubling up a redundant @prefix beside the object .bind() still needs. self.BRICK/self.REF are the SAME situation one level up (bound at lines 12-13) but are not even constructed IN this region -- they come from the sibling region IfcBrickAnnotator.load_brick_schema (same file, same class), where they are themselves `self.X = Namespace(self.settings.value(...))`, i.e. dynamic AND self-exported -- doubly not-expressible, just out of this region's own scope. Went beyond the stratum's own idiom for the rest of the region (INSTRUCTIONS.md §2, 'toujours la construction la plus specifique'), since none of that depends on whether the 5 namespaces above are @prefix or plain objects: the standalone .add() (eq_uri) -> `+{ }`; the two .add() sharing subject pt_uri -> one fused `+{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 }` (add_run_shared_subject's construction); the four .add() sharing subject bacnet_bnode -> likewise fused, moving the `bacnet_bnode rdf:type ref:BACnetReference` triple's write a few lines later (after obj_id_string is computed) so it can join the fused block -- invisible to the isomorphism oracle (order is not part of a graph's identity) and explicitly the kind of contiguous merge INSTRUCTIONS.md's add_run_shared_subject row prescribes, not the 'refactoring' the same section forbids. add_in_loop (this region's second stratum, INSTRUCTIONS.md's own tirage): `for _key, data in self.annotations_registry.items():` with `_key` never read -> `for @bindings as data in self.annotations_registry.values():`. Confirmed by direct experiment with the transpiler (see scratch repro) that `data.raw[key]`/`data.raw.get(key[, default])` behave exactly like the original dict's `data[key]`/`data.get(...)`, including a MISSING key returning None rather than raising -- needed because the original reads are all either a Python truthiness test (`if data.get('bacnet_name'):`, `data.get('ifc_type')`) or a namespace-subscript key (`ifc_inst_ns[data['eq_guid']]`), never an RDF term directly: exactly the `if row[col] != "":`-shaped case INSTRUCTIONS.md §2 bis flags for `.raw` (`Literal('') != ''`). The one place a raw field value becomes an RDF term with no other transformation -- `rdflib.Literal(data.get('bacnet_name'))` -- became `?bacnet_name` (the current @bindings, term-coerced): confirmed by the same scratch repro that a plain string field coerces to an untyped/unlangtagged Literal identical to `rdflib.Literal(str_value)`. New finding, worth flagging beyond this pair: inside a typed-literal's quoted part, `{expr}` does NOT interpolate on its own -- a bare `"{obj_id_string}"^^{dt}` produced the LITERAL TEXT `{obj_id_string}` (an f-string-shaped brace left un-evaluated), verified with the transpiler on a minimal repro. The quoted part must be spelled as an f-string, `f"{obj_id_string}"^^{dt}` -- INSTRUCTIONS.md §1 does say 'The quoted part may be an f-string' but reads, on a first pass, as an optional convenience rather than a requirement for `{expr}` to fire at all; an agent who copies the bare-`{expr}` habit from `+{ }`'s subject/predicate/object positions into a typed literal's string body gets a SILENT wrong translation (valid syntax, wrong value: the literal '{obj_id_string}' instead of 'analog-input,3'), not a transpile error -- this is exactly the kind of thing INSTRUCTIONS.md §5 asks to remit as a defect-or-documentation-gap finding. No context_shim.py: everything the region's own body references beyond rdflib is a self.* attribute (self.BRICK, self.REF, self.settings, self.annotations_registry), supplied by driver.py's _FakeSelf the same way the sibling TestShaclCreateShaclPropertyName_setUp driver supplies its _FakeSelf -- nothing is imported from outside the file that original.py doesn't already import. driver.py reuses that sibling's comparator verbatim (Graph attributes by graphs_isomorphic(), str-subclass attributes -- Namespace/URIRef/Literal -- by value, everything else by vars() recursion) rather than plain ==, per AGENT_BATCH.md's ANTI-VERT-CREUX warning: checked directly by corrupting one predicate (BRICK.isPointOf -> BRICK.isPointOfWRONG) in translated.ldpy and confirming rdfeval check turns FAIL ('call[0].arg[0]: values differ'), then restoring.
